items.title: 27.4.4 Nutritional and Biological Importance of Lipids

source_refs.note: Topic 27.4.4 as printed (PDF 171-172): the book's two paragraphs, the hibernation Did You Know? box and the second Quick Check 27.3 (the book repeats the number), questions only.

blocks.text: A major function of lipids is to serve as a primary source of energy storage in living organisms. They provide more energy per gram than carbohydrates, because when oxidised to carbon dioxide and water, they have a higher caloric value.

blocks.text: Lipids act as solvents for the transport of fat vitamins (A, D, E and K) and help in their absorption in the intestinal cells and later into the bloodstream. We can meet our vitamin requirements by consuming foods that contain these fat-soluble vitamins. These vitamins should be eaten with a bit of healthy fat. Fats provide insulation to the body from water, heat, and electricity due to their non-polar nature.
bold: We can meet our vitamin requirements by consuming foods that contain these fat-soluble vitamins.

blocks.title: Did You Know?
blocks.text: Animals, such as polar bears, reptiles, and amphibians, store extra fat when hibernating. Hibernation is a condition when animals significantly slow down their metabolic rate, body temperature, heart rate and breathing to save energy for the periods when food is scarce. During this period, metabolic rates decrease extremely. Fat is a more concentrated source of energy compared to glycogen, allowing animals to utilize stored fat effectively while minimizing energy consumption.

blocks.prompt: a) Why lipids are not soluble in water?
blocks.explanation: Their long hydrocarbon chains are non-polar (hydrophobic) and cannot form hydrogen bonds with water molecules.

blocks.prompt: b) What are three major functions of lipids in the human body?
blocks.explanation: Any three: energy storage; insulation and protection of organs; part of cell membranes (phospholipids); solvent for fat-soluble vitamins; hormones (steroids).

blocks.prompt: c) What type/s of lipid do/does not contain fatty acids? Give examples.
blocks.explanation: Steroids (such as cholesterol) and terpenes (such as limonene) do not contain fatty acids. Triglycerides (fats and oils), waxes and phospholipids do contain fatty acids.

blocks.prompt: d) Vegetable oil and vegetable ghee both are triglycerides. What is the major structural difference between the two?
blocks.explanation: The fatty acids of vegetable oil are mostly unsaturated (contain C=C bonds), so it is a liquid. Vegetable ghee is made by hydrogenation of the oil (adding hydrogen across the double bonds), so its fatty acids are mostly saturated and it is a solid.
